request.prompt:
Create an engaging two-minute cinematic YouTube documentary titled
"The Internet Is Under the Ocean."

Begin with a powerful three-second hook showing someone sending a message.
Reveal that the wireless connection is only the beginning and that the
information may travel through physical fiber-optic cables beneath the ocean.

Explain the journey from the viewer's device to a router, terrestrial fiber,
a coastal cable landing station, an undersea cable, and another continent.
Explain how light carries information through protected glass fibers.

Make cable damage and repair the most suspenseful section. Show relevant
oceans, coastlines, fiber-optic equipment, cable-laying ships, cable reels,
technicians, landing facilities, server infrastructure, and data centers.

Use only relevant images and authentic video clips with subtitles. Do not use
charts, diagrams, statement cards, animated templates, fake interfaces, or
generic unrelated technology footage.

Use a strong opening hook, curiosity gaps, natural cause-and-effect
transitions, and a memorable closing payoff. Write natural documentary
narration for a general audience. Do not read headings or production
instructions aloud. Do not invent statistics, cable names, capacities,
distances, dates, companies, or repair times.

Target approximately 120 seconds. Keep visual changes synchronized with
meaningful narration boundaries. Avoid excessive cuts, repeated assets,
unrelated visuals, blank frames, and abruptly cut narration.

creative.audience: Curious adults interested in technology and engineering
